title: ASUS AI Agent Computers: The Complete Guide to Local AI PCs
summary: Learn how to choose an ASUS agent computer for local AI, from NUC mini PCs and RTX 5090 builds to GX10 systems and enterprise AI workstations.
body_markdown:
**Your own AI, running on your own box, 24/7.** An agent computer doesn't just chat. It actually does stuff: digs through your files, drafts the email, writes the script and runs it. Run it locally on ASUS hardware and your data stays on your machine, with no per-token bill every time an agent spins up. ASUS covers everything from a tiny NUC to a dual RTX PRO 6000 workstation with 192GB of VRAM, and you can grab the parts on Newegg.


So what should you actually get? Mostly it comes down to how big a model you want to run:


-


**Just want to tinker:** an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB (or a Radeon AI PRO R9700 32GB if you want more VRAM headroom) plus 32–64GB of DDR5. Plenty for a local chatbot, doc Q&A and a coding copilot, and no monthly subscription.


-


**Building and fine-tuning:** an RTX 5090 32GB with 128GB of DDR5. Or skip the tower and put an ASUS Ascent GX10 on your desk: NVIDIA DGX Spark with 128GB of unified memory, in a box that fits next to your monitor.


-


**Homelab, always on:** two RTX 5090s on an ROG Crosshair X870E or ROG Maximus Z890 with 256GB of DDR5. Your own private AI server, and it keeps working while you sleep.


-


**Running it for a team:** a Pro WS WRX90E-SAGE SE or W890E-SAGE SE with RTX PRO 6000 96GB cards. It serves 70B+ models to up to 50 people, and nothing leaves the building.


## What is an AI agent computer?


An agent computer is a PC that runs AI agents — software that can pursue a goal by itself, decide the next step and carry out several steps in sequence, often around the clock. A chatbot answers; an agent acts: it reads your files, drafts replies, runs scripts and calls tools on your behalf.


ASUS frames the case for running agents locally in three points ([ASUS](https://www.asus.com/us/site/agent-computer/?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_asus-ai-agent-computers-the-complete-guide-to-local-ai-pcs) ):


-


**Flexible data control:** sensitive data stays on your hardware across local, hybrid and cloud setups.


-


**Lower total cost:** small language models (SLMs) run locally, cutting recurring cloud API token spend.


-


**Unchained performance:** hardware built for 24/7 automated agents and multi-agent "swarms".


**What matters most in hardware:** memory first (GPU VRAM plus system RAM decides which model size fits), then fast NVMe storage for model files, then sustained cooling for always-on workloads.


**Agent software ASUS supports:** ASUS Zenni Claw (guided agent assistant with local-cloud routing), NVIDIA NemoClaw (safety-hardened agent stack for RTX PCs and DGX Spark), Intel SuperClaw (CPU/NPU-first runtime for Core Ultra), AMD ROCm.AI, and Nous Research Hermes Agent (200+ LLMs). ASUS EZ Installer sets up OpenClaw on ASUS mini PCs and NUCs in one click.

## How to choose your agent computer


Start from the largest model you want to run, then buy enough GPU memory (or unified memory) to hold it. As a rule of thumb, a 4-bit (Q4) model needs roughly 0.6GB of memory per billion parameters plus room for context; these figures are approximate.

**Three checks before you buy:**


1.


**Memory:** VRAM sets the model size; system RAM should be at least 2x VRAM for offloading and RAG indexes (ASUS pairs 32GB VRAM with 128GB DDR5).


2.


**Storage:** model files run 5–150GB each, so start with a 2–4TB PCIe 5.0 NVMe drive.


3.


**Cooling and power:** agents run 24/7, so plan for sustained load — a 1000W+ PSU for one RTX 5090, 1600W for two.


**Laptop or desktop?** Choose a ProArt or ROG laptop when you need agents on the go; choose a custom PC or Ascent GX10 when the agent runs around the clock as a home or office AI server.


## FAQ


### What is an AI agent computer?


A PC built to run AI agents locally — software that pursues a goal, decides its next step and completes multi-step tasks on your behalf, often around the clock.


### Why run AI agents locally instead of in the cloud?


Local agents keep sensitive data on your own hardware and cut recurring cloud API token costs. ASUS supports local, hybrid and cloud setups, so you can route only heavy tasks to the cloud.


### What is the best ASUS computer for running local LLMs?


For 7B–32B models, an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RTX 5090 32GB build on an ASUS ROG motherboard. For 32B–120B models, the ASUS Ascent GX10 with 128GB unified memory. For 70B+ models serving teams, a Pro WS WRX90E-SAGE SE workstation with RTX PRO 6000 96GB GPUs.


### What is the ASUS Ascent GX10?


A compact desktop AI supercomputer built on NVIDIA DGX Spark with the GB10 Superchip and 128GB LPDDR5x unified memory. Two units can be linked with a QSFP cable. It is sold on Newegg in 1TB and 4TB versions.


### How much RAM do I need for an AI agent PC?


ASUS pairs 32–64GB DDR5 with Personal AI builds, 128GB with AI Development builds, 256GB with dual-GPU homelab builds, and up to 2TB R-DIMM with enterprise workstations.


### Which agent software runs on ASUS PCs?


ASUS Zenni Claw, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Intel SuperClaw, AMD ROCm.AI and Nous Research Hermes Agent. ASUS EZ Installer sets up OpenClaw on ASUS mini PCs and NUCs in one click.


### Can a mini PC run AI agents?


Yes. ASUS NUC 15 Pro+ (Core Ultra 9 285H, up to 99 TOPS) handles CPU/NPU-first agents with small models, and the ROG NUC 16 with an RTX 5080 Laptop GPU handles larger GPU-accelerated models.


### Where can I buy ASUS agent computer hardware?


Newegg.com carries ASUS motherboards, GPUs, NUC mini PCs, the Ascent GX10 and the memory and NVMe storage to complete a local AI build.
